children: Shares of Adeia plunged after the company cut its full-year outlook and reported a decline in third-quarter revenue that surprised Wall Street analysts.
Shares fell 23% to $16.02 in after-hours trading on Monday. The stock closed down 3.6% at $20.67, and was up 20% this year through the close.

The technology and intellectual‑property licensing company said it expects to generate $375 million to $415 million in revenue this year, a $20 million drop from its previous guidance. It also said it expects a lower profit this year than it had previously forecast.
Chief Financial Officer Keith Jones said that the company's revenue this year may be impacted by the timing of certain deals.

"We remain confident in our ability to achieve the high end of our revenue guidance range for 2026," Jones said. "However, we felt it prudent to adjust the range to reflect the potential impact to the extent certain of these deals are executed beyond the end of the year."
The lowered outlook came as Adeia reported a profit of $2.3 million, or 2 cents a share, compared with a profit of $8.8 million, or 8 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted earnings were 21 cents a share. Analysts polled by FactSet expected 30 cents a share.
Revenue fell to $80.2 million from $87.3 million a year earlier. Analysts were looking for revenue to grow to $98.9 million.
